title: Isomorphism criterion for complete local algebras with flat target
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, and let $(C,\mathfrak c)$ and $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for their respective maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $A\to C$ and $A\to B$ be local homomorphisms (they send $\mathfrak m$ into $\mathfrak c$ and $\mathfrak n$), and let $\phi:C\to B$ be a local $A$-algebra homomorphism. Suppose $B$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and the induced homomorphism $C/\mathfrak mC\to B/\mathfrak mB$ is an isomorphism. Then $\phi$ is injective, $\mathfrak cB=\mathfrak n$, the residue-field map $C/\mathfrak c\to B/\mathfrak n$ is an isomorphism, $B$ is a finite $C$-module via $\phi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $1\in B$ generates it. Consequently $\phi$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras. No flatness of $C$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, final paragraph: the complete-local algebra criterion extracted from its injectivity and surjectivity arguments.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-mod-injective] with $R=A$, $S=C$, $N=C$, $M=B$, and $u=\phi$. The map $A\to C$ is local, $C$ is Noetherian, and $N=C$ is generated over $C$ by $1$. The target $B$ is $A$-flat, and the reduction of $u$ is injective by the assumed fibre isomorphism. Thus $\phi$ is injective. In particular, this application requires no flatness of $C$ over $A$.

source.place: Tag 00ME, lemma-mod-injective; apply to the underlying A-linear map C to B

proof.text: Locality gives $\mathfrak mB\subseteq\mathfrak cB\subseteq\mathfrak n$. For $b\in\mathfrak n$, surjectivity on the closed fibre gives $c\in C$ with $b-\phi(c)\in\mathfrak mB$. Then $\phi(c)\in\mathfrak n$; if $c\notin\mathfrak c$, it is a unit, whose image is a unit, a contradiction. Hence $c\in\mathfrak c$ and $b\in\mathfrak cB$, proving $\mathfrak cB=\mathfrak n$. The same fibre lifting proves surjectivity of $C/\mathfrak c\to B/\mathfrak n$. Its kernel is zero: $\phi(c)\in\mathfrak n$ forces $c\in\mathfrak c$ by the unit argument. Thus this residue map is an isomorphism and the class of $1$ generates $B/\mathfrak cB$ over $C/\mathfrak c$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, final paragraph; elementary closed-fibre and residue calculation

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], completeness of $B$ gives $\bigcap_{r\ge1}\mathfrak n^r=0$. Since $\mathfrak cB=\mathfrak n$, the $C$-submodule $\mathfrak c^rB$ equals $(\mathfrak cB)^r=\mathfrak n^r$ (expand products of ideal generators). Hence $\bigcap_{r\ge1}\mathfrak c^rB=0$. The same definition says that $C$ is $\mathfrak c$-adically complete, as required for the next step.

source.place: Tag 0317, definition-complete, applied to B and C

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] with ring $C$, ideal $\mathfrak c$, and module $B$ via $\phi$. Completeness and separation were checked in Step 3. Step 2 gives that $B/\mathfrak cB$ is generated by the image of $1$, so it is finite over $C/\mathfrak c$. The lemma gives that $B$ is finite over $C$ and, by its precise generator clause, that $1$ generates $B$ over $C$.

source.place: Tag 031D, lemma-finite-over-complete-ring, including the chosen-generator conclusion established in its proof

proof.text: Generation by $1$ means every $b\in B$ is $c\cdot1=\phi(c)$ for some $c\in C$, so $\phi$ is surjective. Together with Step 1 it is bijective. Its inverse preserves addition, multiplication, the unit and the $A$-algebra structure by applying the injective map $\phi$ to each required identity. Thus $\phi$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras, with all the preceding clauses already proved.
